name: reserved-id-override-reconciliation
description: Remote agent registrations may shadow a built-in pipeline id ONLY as a deliberate, authenticated operator act - and the override must never touch the compile-time blueprint map.
principles: Remote dispatch wins at the executor, so an id-9 registration redirects every prompt call: default-deny, allow only with allow_builtin_override AND a valid session.

The override lives in the RemotePipelines entry alone; the compile-time blueprint map (PIPELINE_INFO) is never seeded, overwritten, or stubbed for built-in ids - seeding an empty blueprint there corrupts built-in dispatch and crashed the host.
Deregister restores built-in dispatch instantly because the blueprint was never touched.
Registration guards are three-key: id reserved?, flag set?, session valid? - all three decide; any refusal logs its real reason.
heuristics: When wiring any override/escape-hatch path: enumerate what the normal path writes, and exclude destructive writes for the overridden entity.
Test the allowed path in isolation (kill competing walk load first): the first allowed-override test coincided with a memory-pressure death and needed a clean re-run.

decision_rules.condition: a remote registration names a built-in pipeline id
decision_rules.action: Refuse unless allow_builtin_override AND valid session; if allowed, register the remote entry only - never seed or modify the blueprint map.
Built-in dispatch restores with no further action; verify via the remote list being empty for that id.
